title: Sunny and the Banksia Pods | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka finds a cluster of ancient banksia pods on a moonlit bush path — each one a perfect wooden sculpture that has held a thousand seeds and seen a hundred seasons. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny picked up the banksia pod from the path.

It was old. She could tell just by the weight of it — heavy and woody and dense, as if it had been storing up time along with everything else. Its surface was rough and ridged and covered in small follicles — dozens of tiny mouths, most of them open now, their seeds long since released.

She turned it slowly in her paws.

Each of those open follicles had once held a seed. Each seed had gone somewhere — carried by the wind, by fire, by water, by a creature like her passing through the bush.

She thought: this one pod has already sent out so many new things into the world.

The pod was as big as her head. She held it gently, the way she might hold something precious, because it was.

She sat down with it on the path and held it in her lap. The moonlight caught its rough grey surface and made it look almost silver.

All those little mouths.

All those seeds gone out into the dark, into the soil, into the wind.

Some of them had become trees. Some of them had become the very bush she was sitting in right now.

She set the pod down carefully and leaned against a nearby tree.

The banksia pod sat there in the moonlight, saying nothing, having already said everything.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, banksia pod. Goodnight, little one.
